# Portfolio Analytics

A portfolio-tracking application that reconstructs a full investment history —
holdings, cash, income, fees, and returns — from source statements, and
serves it through a typed API to a React/D3 frontend.

This repository is a **public release copy**. It runs entirely against a
**synthetic, fictional dataset** generated by its own code (`tools/generate_demo_data.py`);
it contains no real financial data, real filenames, or personal information.
The engine, reconciliation, and API layers are exactly what the private
development version runs — nothing about the accounting logic is
demo-specific. See [Validation philosophy](#validation-philosophy) below.

## What it does

- Parses source statements (PDF and CSV) into a normalised, provenance-tracked
  transaction ledger — every figure traces back to the document, page, and
  extraction method that produced it.
- Reconciles multiple sources of the same events (e.g. a CSV export and a PDF
  statement covering overlapping periods) into one deterministic,
  authoritative ledger, with an explicit, machine-readable record of *why*
  each source was trusted or superseded.
- Runs a from-scratch accounting engine over that ledger: holdings and cost
  basis, cash balance, time-weighted and money-weighted (XIRR) returns,
  income, fees, and reconciliation against the source's own reported figures.
- Rebuilds a full daily history (balances, drawdowns, milestones, allocation
  over time) and exposes it, plus a set of derived analytics (attribution,
  concentration, contribution-to-return), through a versioned FastAPI service.
- Renders it all in a React + D3 frontend: an overview, a performance page,
  holdings and allocation, income, gains, contributions, risk, and a full
  activity/history view — with a light/dark theme that follows the OS by
  default.

## Architecture

```
statements (PDF/CSV)
        │
        ▼
  src/ingestion/        parse source documents into structured records,
                         redacting/stripping anything identity-bearing
        │
        ▼
  src/normalisation/     map source vocabulary onto a canonical transaction
                         type system
        │
        ▼
  src/models/            the canonical domain model (Transaction, Security,
                         Holding, ...), Decimal-typed throughout
        │
        ▼
  src/engine/            an in-memory ledger + engines: holdings, cash,
                         cost basis, returns, reconciliation against the
                         source's own reported figures
        │
        ▼
  src/history/           replays the engine day-by-day into a stored
                         history: balances, drawdowns, milestones,
                         allocation over time
        │
        ▼
  src/analytics/         derived views over that history: attribution,
                         concentration, income, gains, contributions
        │
        ▼
  src/api/                a FastAPI service exposing all of the above as
                         typed JSON
        │
        ▼
  web/                    a React 19 + TypeScript + D3 frontend — it renders
                         what the API returns and performs no financial
                         calculations of its own
```

Multi-source ingestion (`src/ingestion/vanguard_csv/`) is a separate track:
independently parsing a CSV export of the same account, matching its trades
against the PDF-derived ledger, and reconciling the two into a single
promoted set of transactions with an explicit source-authority policy. It's
included here as engineering evidence of that reconciliation design — see
[docs/source-reconciliation.md](docs/source-reconciliation.md) and
[docs/vanguard-csv-ingestion.md](docs/vanguard-csv-ingestion.md) — but the
demo dataset in this repository is seeded directly (see below), not by
running that reconciliation against real exports.

## Key engineering decisions

- **Canonical events, not source-shaped rows.** Every ingestion path
  (PDF or CSV) converts into the same small `Transaction`/`TxnType` model
  before anything downstream ever sees it. The engine has no idea which
  source a transaction came from.
- **Explicit source authority, not silent overwrite.** When two sources
  cover the same event, promoting one over the other is a recorded decision
  (`SourceAuthorityPolicy`), not an implicit "last write wins" — see
  `src/ingestion/vanguard_csv/reconcile.py`.
- **A trade is two events, not one.** A buy/sell affects both holdings
  (units, cost basis) and cash (the settlement). Representing it as a single
  row with implicit cash effects made the cash engine's `CASH_TYPES` set
  ambiguous; instead a trade always produces a `BUY`/`SELL` row *and* a
  paired `TRANSFER` row for its cash leg, with brokerage broken out as its
  own `FEE` row.
- **Deposit reversals are ordinary transactions, not a special case.** A
  reversed/dishonoured deposit is just a second transaction with the
  opposite sign, dated when the reversal was recorded — no separate
  "reversal" code path exists anywhere in the engine.
- **Money is `Decimal`, end to end.** Every monetary value is a Python
  `Decimal`, serialised as an exact string over the API — never a float,
  anywhere in the pipeline.
- **The frontend does no accounting.** It renders whatever the API returns.
  Every number on screen — a return, a balance, an allocation weight — was
  computed once, in `src/engine/` or `src/analytics/`, and nowhere else.

## Validation philosophy

This project was originally built and validated against a real personal
Vanguard account. That validation — real balances, real reconciliation
results, real accuracy figures against the broker's own reported numbers —
is what actually proves the accounting engine is correct, but it is
**private** and does not appear anywhere in this repository, its history, or
its test fixtures.

What *is* here is a parallel, fully synthetic validation path:

- `tools/generate_demo_data.py` builds a fictional multi-year portfolio —
  deposits, a reversed deposit, buys, sells, a withdrawal, dividends, ETF
  distributions, interest, admin fees, brokerage, and a fee reversal, across
  five fictional securities — and runs it through the **exact same**
  ingestion → matching → canonicalisation → seeding path the real pipeline
  uses (see `seed_transactions_from_candidates` in
  `src/ingestion/vanguard_csv/promote.py`), not a hand-written fixture of
  final numbers.
- `tests/tools/test_generate_demo_data.py` asserts that build is
  deterministic, that cash never goes negative, and that the engine's own
  reconciliation checks pass against the demo's own reported snapshots.
- The rest of the test suite (`tests/`) is entirely synthetic fixtures and
  unit tests of individual engine rules (cost-basis methods, distribution
  vs. dividend classification, brokerage-inclusive net amounts, reversal
  pairing, ...). A handful of tests that exercise the real portfolio
  (`test_real_data_smoke.py` and similar) are written to `pytest.skip()`
  gracefully when the private source files they need aren't present — which,
  in this checkout, they never are.

In short: **the numbers you'll see running this repository are fictional,
but the code computing them is identical to the code that was validated
against real data.**

## Tech stack

- **Backend:** Python 3.14, FastAPI 0.141, Uvicorn, SQLite (via a thin
  repository layer, no ORM), pdfplumber for PDF extraction, pytest.
- **Frontend:** React 19, TypeScript, Vite 8, D3 7 for charts, TanStack Query
  5 for data fetching/caching, react-router-dom 7, CSS Modules. Storybook +
  Vitest + Testing Library for component tests; `tsc` and oxlint for static
  checks.

## Running locally

No private data, account, or API key is required — everything below runs
against the synthetic dataset committed at `demo-data/portfolio.demo.db`.

### Backend

```bash
python3 -m venv venv
./venv/bin/pip install -r requirements.txt -r requirements-dev.txt
PORTFOLIO_DB_PATH=demo-data/portfolio.demo.db ./venv/bin/uvicorn src.api.app:app --reload
```

The API is now serving on `http://localhost:8000`.

To confirm the test suite and the demo build both work:

```bash
./venv/bin/pytest -q
./venv/bin/python -m tools.generate_demo_data   # regenerate the demo dataset (deterministic)
```

### Frontend

```bash
cd web
npm install --legacy-peer-deps   # see note below
npm run dev
```

Then open `http://localhost:5173`.

> **Note:** this repository's frontend dependency tree currently has one
> unresolved peer-dependency conflict between Storybook 10's addon-vitest and
> `@vitest/browser` (both dev-only, unrelated to the running app), which
> requires `--legacy-peer-deps` on install. `npm run build`, `npm test`, and
> `tsc --noEmit` all pass cleanly once installed.

### Everything at once

```bash
./venv/bin/pytest -q && (cd web && npm run build)
```

## What this is not

This is a personal-project demonstration, not a production financial
product. In particular, it does not (and does not claim to):

- connect live to any brokerage or bank — all data is manually-sourced
  statements, ingested offline;
- support multiple users, accounts, or authentication;
- provide investment, tax, or financial advice;
- benchmark against a market index (returns shown are the portfolio's own,
  not compared to anything external).

## Project layout

```
src/            backend: ingestion, normalisation, models, engine, history,
                analytics, api (see Architecture above)
tools/          the synthetic demo-data generator
tests/          backend test suite (entirely synthetic fixtures)
web/            frontend: React + TypeScript + D3
docs/           design and engineering notes written during development
demo-data/      the committed synthetic demo database
```
